# Claude Code parity matrix

Generated from the machine-readable capability manifest. One symbol per capability,
derived from four orthogonal dimensions (`recognized` / `mounted` / `behavioral` / `ux`):

- ✅ full parity: behavior matches upstream, mounted by default, complete UX
- 🔶 partial: usable with known differences (see Deviation/Notes)
- ❌ missing: absent today
- 🚫 not a parity port — may exist as a dsh-native equivalent (see Deviations)

## Subagents

| Status | Capability | Recognized | Mounted | Behavior | UX | Evidence | Deviation | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🔶 | <a id="cap-subagents.task-tool"></a>Subagents / Agent tool / teams | ✓ | ✓ | Divergent | Partial | [s1](packages/preset/cc/agent.cordis.yml) [s2](packages/preset/cc/agent.cordis.yml) [t1](packages/subagent/task/tests/tool.spec.ts) [t2](packages/subagent/task/tests/epoch-collector.spec.ts) [t3](packages/subagent/task/tests/suppress-settled.spec.ts) [t4](packages/subagent/task/tests/integration.spec.ts) [t5](packages/subagent/task/tests/registry-publication.spec.ts) [s3](packages/subagent/task/src/preload-tools.ts) [t6](packages/subagent/task/tests/preload-tools.spec.ts) [t7](packages/ui/tui/tests/promote-key.spec.ts) [t8](packages/subagent/resume-pins/tests/gate.spec.ts) [t9](packages/bundle/cc-shell/tests/resume-pins-composition.spec.ts) | divergent — subagent_type dispatch over per-workspace .claude/agents (persona = definition systemPrompt, alias routing via ccModelRoutes, sanitized toolFilter, maxDepth 3, bundled explore/dsh-cc-guide agents, the bundled explore additionally carrying read-only serena symbol retrieval tools mcp__serena__find_symbol / find_referencing_symbols / get_symbols_overview) plus the continuable background loop (run_in_background, agentId-addressable send_message/interrupt/list). Deliberate deviations: fork + background is rejected naming upstream issue #2124 (fork stays foreground one-shot); no TaskOutput alias and no outputFile field; omitting run_in_background stays foreground unless the definition pins background: true, unlike Claude Code's interactive omit=background. Pinned defaults (repo-guarded): the repo agents deep-reasoner and fast-worker pin background: true, so omitting run_in_background on those Task calls launches them continuable in the background (the call resolves { status: 'async_launched' } immediately and the real result arrives later as a wake message — no inline result to compose on); run_in_background: false forces synchronous collection. Deliberate deviation: there is NO global omit=background default — the bundled explore and dsh-cc-guide agents stay unpinned and keep foreground first-epoch collect. Foreground collect refit: non-fork foreground calls (named agents and general-purpose) collect the child's first epoch INLINE as a continuable child — same pin preallocation, pre-start pin write, and tombstone-on-throw as the background path, so a foreground-launched child is pinnable/resumable exactly like a background one. The collector is a dsh-cc-INTERNAL parity instrument (bus watcher over subagent/start + subagent/end, one shared listener pair and watch map, matched by first-epoch runId; docs/plans/ 2026-09-10-epoch-collector-dsh-cc.md), NOT a Claude Code mechanism — declared deviations: (1) for inline-collected epochs the settlement account lives only in the tool result, not the parent session log (the duplicated subagent-settled notice is dropped by a pop-once pre-step filter; a promoted child is removed from the set and delivers normally); (2) on exec.signal abort the child is interrupted aborted exactly once via ctx.subagents.interrupt({kind:'ancestor'}) and the tool call resolves PROMPTLY with a synthetic stopReason "aborted" (never awaiting child quiescence; the real terminal arrives only as the suppressed notice); (3) a seam without interrupt degrades to a prompt resolve without child interrupt. Output schema gains optional backgroundedByUser: true (set by the Slice 3 promotion path, never by Slice 2 code paths). Ctrl+B promotion (TUI-only surface): while the dialog is busy AND the root-realm ccCollectorRegistry (published by the cc-subagent-task plugin, CcPlugins pattern) has ≥1 armed foreground collect for THIS session AND CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS is unset, Ctrl+B promotes EVERY armed collect of the session: the pending tool call resolves { status: 'async_launched', agentId, backgroundedByUser: true }, the watch is released (the runId-matched end later resolves nothing), the child is REMOVED from the suppression set so its settlement notice delivers exactly once normally, and the TUI echoes one status line. Pre-acceptance promotion (Ctrl+B fired while startContinuable is still in flight) resolves async_launched as soon as start resolves. Repeated presses are idempotent (a promoted collect unregisters itself; the second press is a consumed no-op). Declared deviations: promotion is a TUI-only surface — non-TUI clients have NO promotion path; busy Esc/Ctrl+C still interrupts (every registered collect of the session aborts exactly-once with a prompt synthetic aborted resolution); idle Ctrl+B is untouched (the editor's tui.editor.cursorLeft binding); under tmux, Ctrl+B is the default prefix — double-press passes a literal Ctrl+B through (send-prefix) and the Ctrl+X Ctrl+B chord is P1 (not implemented). Env kill switch CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS: a non-empty value other than case-insensitive 0/false disables the backgrounding-by-default pins (omissions collect in foreground) — explicit run_in_background true/false arguments remain honored both ways. Deliberate partial-parity deviation: upstream Claude Code's exact precedence for this env var is unverified, so the argument precedence is declared rather than asserted as parity. Capacity guard: the Task tool refuses a new continuable child (background OR foreground collect) when the parent already has 25 live children (listChildren entries with activity running) with the actionable error "parent has 25 live subagents; /agents stop <id> to release one, or let children settle" — a dsh-cc-side safety valve; Claude Code has no equivalent surfaced limit. Continuable cold resume: each background spawn captures a resume pin (resolveDetailed-selected alias plus maxTokens) into the resumePinStore service (preset row cc-resume-pins, isolated as resumePinStore in cc-services), and resume restores the pinned tuple INCLUDING explicit absence (a pin recording an unset reasoningEffort/maxTokens is honored as absent rather than re-resolved); a pinned model the parent can no longer resolve is gated by the subagents-resume settings namespace (subagents-resume.onUnavailableModel: block\|route-current, default block) with deny codes SUBAGENT_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE / WORKSPACE_CHANGED / DEFINITION_CHANGED / PINNED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE / PIN_ORPHANED / PIN_UNREADABLE naming the policy knob — Claude Code has no equivalent mechanism. Spawn-time preload (dsh-cc-side, no Claude Code equivalent): an explicit `tools:` entry that is still a deferred MCP tool is activated through the duck-typed ctx.toolSearch seam at spawn, BEFORE the child starts, on BOTH dispatch paths — activation is process-global (every admitting agent's schema grows after the spawn); wildcard entries are restrict-only, deny/sanitize-excluded names are never activated, eager names are skipped, and outcomes surface in the Task result text (Preloaded deferred tools for child / Not preloaded: name (reason)). | — |

| Status | Capability | Recognized | Mounted | Behavior | UX | Evidence | Deviation | Notes |

| 🔶 | <a id="cap-permissions.rules"></a>Permission rules | ✓ | ✓ | Partial | Partial | [t1](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/mode.spec.ts) [t2](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/classifier.spec.ts) [t3](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/auto-stage.spec.ts) [t4](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/listener-auto-stage.spec.ts) [t5](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/llm-classifier.spec.ts) [t6](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/llm-classifier.spec.ts) [t7](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/auto-stage.spec.ts) [t8](packages/ui/tui/tests/driver-classifier-breaker.spec.ts) [s1](packages/interaction/permission-rules/src/auto-stage.ts) [t9](packages/settings/settings-cascade/tests/auto-mode.spec.ts) [t10](packages/ui/tui/tests/approval-preview.spec.ts) [t11](packages/ui/tui/tests/driver-default-mode.spec.ts) [t12](packages/interaction/permission-rules/tests/permission-rules.spec.ts) | downgrade — Rule engine + dangerous-command/path risk classifier, durable modes (default/acceptEdits/plan/auto/bypassPermissions via /permissions), plan deny with exit_plan_mode guidance, bypassPermissions pinning danger-full-access with resumeSandbox restore, and the always-allow derived-rule persistence all work. `auto` mode additionally gains an opt-in, escalate-only LLM risk-classifier stage: a one-shot auxiliary model verdict over tool name + rendered parameters (never tool results, input wrapped as an explicit DATA block the model is instructed never to repeat, quote, or follow), fail-to-ask on every classifier failure, `$defaults` soft-deny prose expansion, a verdict LRU cache, and durable `permission/classifier` session audit events (armed only when enabled, an llm service is mounted, and the alias route resolves). Read-only tool calls are exempt: they never invoke the classifier (the legacy auto path applies). Verdict parsing stays strict and fail-closed — a malformed output yields the constant reason "classifier output unparseable" (model output never reaches the modal; the audit record is digest-only). A per-route consecutive-failure circuit breaker (threshold 3, keyed provider/model) opens the stage for a failing lane: no further classifier calls on that route, one warn per process, one `breaker` audit event per session, reset by a settings change (rebuild). The breaker is restart-durable within a session: the first call of a session seeds the per-route streak from the durable log (attributed events only; a restored streak ≥ threshold opens at seed time). An open breaker surfaces one visible TUI fallback notice per session (live-appended `breaker` events only — never replayed logs), and caller-cancelled classifications are tagged `cancelled`, never breaker-counted. Raw model output is debuggable via the opt-in `DSH_PERMISSION_CLASSIFIER_DEBUG=1` process-log channel (`[dsh:classifier:raw]`, truncated to 2 KiB — never session events). Defaults: `timeoutMs` 8000, verdict budget 1024 tokens. The UI honors `permissions.defaultMode`: statusline, session switch, Shift+Tab cycle start, and the /permissions picker all fall back to the live merged settings default (fold precedence — a recorded session mode still wins), with the cycle clamped to its members. Settings-surface deviation: the auto-mode section is delivered as `permissions.autoMode` — an `autoMode` key inside the existing `permissions` namespace (camelCase key in a kebab namespace, like `defaultMode`), NOT Claude Code's root-level `autoMode` key, because top-level settings namespaces must be kebab-case upstream. Other documented CC auto-mode divergences (explicit ask rules still proxied to allow in auto; same-source allow-before-deny) remain recorded as unfixed follow-ups — they are not addressed or masked here. Remaining vs CC: managed/enterprise remote settings, UI mode cycle; the upstream permission/mode catalog pin is an upstream polish. | — |

## Deviations and known limits

- <a id="dev-engine.bash-jobs"></a>`engine.bash-jobs` — downgrade: CC's TaskCreate/TaskOutput/TaskStop tool naming is not aliased; the dsh jobs tools (tool-jobs over the host job registry) carry the equivalent surface under dsh names.
- <a id="dev-engine.cost-tracking"></a>`engine.cost-tracking` — downgrade: Ships an empty default price table (composition decides pricing), and CC quota/limit surfaces are vendor-billing-bound — the TUI /usage panel footnotes quota as unavailable.
- <a id="dev-engine.credentials"></a>`engine.credentials` — downgrade: FORCED DOWNGRADE at seed: the row is genuinely ✅ via the host-plane upstream package dsh-credentials-local, but that package has no in-repo file to anchor a positive claim against, so per the evidence backfill rule the claim is downgraded until an in-repo seam exists.
- <a id="dev-engine.ide-lsp"></a>`engine.ide-lsp` — downgrade: Two paths. Production: Serena MCP via user-scope ~/.claude.json (v1.7.0 pin) — symbol-level retrieval/editing/diagnostics, ~30 tools deferred through ToolSearch; gaps: no hover tool, no call hierarchy, no push diagnostics. Native dsh-lsp/dsh-lsp-stdio/dsh-tool-lsp exist with a closed 4-operation read-only seam but are NOT mounted by any shipped composition (no lsp rows in cordis.patch.yml/agent.cordis.yml). cc-plugin-loader does not parse lspServers/.lsp.json manifests; PreToolUse hooks ignore additionalContext. /ide and editor pods remain host-shell scope; headless does not apply.
- <a id="dev-engine.notifications"></a>`engine.notifications` — upstream-blocked (upstream_dependency: notification-seam): No notification seam in deepseek-harness; needs a new design.
- <a id="dev-engine.onboarding"></a>`engine.onboarding` — downgrade: No package or design doc exists for onboarding/tips.
- <a id="dev-engine.remote-sessions"></a>`engine.remote-sessions` — downgrade: FORCED DOWNGRADE at seed: the legacy row reads "🔶 different — CC bridge/ is claude.ai-bound; dsh has its own web/host/sdk/acp stack outside this repo", but that stack has no in-repo surface to anchor a positive claim against, so the seed records the four dimensions as non-positive until the external stack gains an in-repo seam.
- <a id="dev-engine.sandbox"></a>`engine.sandbox` — downgrade: FORCED DOWNGRADE at seed: the row is genuinely ✅ via the host-plane upstream packages dsh-sandbox-local + policy, but they have no in-repo file to anchor a positive claim against, so per the evidence backfill rule the claim is downgraded until an in-repo seam exists.
- <a id="dev-engine.schedule"></a>`engine.schedule` — downgrade: after_seconds / at / every_seconds (>=300s) supported; CC's cron-expression selectors are unsupported until the dsh-schedule selector seam lands (upstream extension planned).
- <a id="dev-engine.tui"></a>`engine.tui` — downgrade: dsh --profile tui is the terminal surface: Shift+Tab mode cycling, Esc interrupt, Ctrl+C/Ctrl+S/Ctrl+T/Ctrl+O/Up/Tab bindings, approval previews with 1/2/3 answers on a shared FIFO, leading-! bash mode with separate history, TUI-local /export-md /copy /usage, six-role theme, context-occupancy statusline, custom statusLine and multi-hunk diff transcript rendering. Vim mode and ghost text are still later; the statusLine contract's remaining limits are detailed in ux.statusline.
- <a id="dev-engine.vendor-internals"></a>`engine.vendor-internals` — non-goal: Anthropic-internal or vendor-bound features; no design asset and out of parity scope.
- <a id="dev-engine.voice"></a>`engine.voice` — non-goal: Vendor feature with no design asset; won't port.
- <a id="dev-engine.web-fetch"></a>`engine.web-fetch` — downgrade: Mounted via @dsh-cc/tool-web-fetch (optional prompt summarized on resolve('haiku'); prompt without haiku hard-fails before fetch). Fetch executor is @dsh-cc/web-fetch-http wrapping HttpFetchProvider, mounted from cc-shell. WebFetch(domain:) content rules match hostnames. Literal SSRF gate blocks private/loopback/ link-local literals. Residual: no DNS pinning, no Anthropic preflight, no 15-min cache, no pre-approved docs domains; upstream webfetch-ssrf-allowlist remains for DNS-pin / per-hop re-validation.
- <a id="dev-hooks.executors"></a>`hooks.executors` — downgrade: command + http (SSRF-allowlisted via allowedHttpHookUrls) executors are always on; prompt/agent executors are gated behind enablePromptHooks / enableAgentHooks (default off) and resolve their model: through ccModelRoutes (omitted model → the haiku cheap lane).
- <a id="dev-hooks.message-display"></a>`hooks.message-display` — downgrade: Not bridged — no dsh emit point for message-display rendering events.
- <a id="dev-hooks.notification"></a>`hooks.notification` — downgrade: Bridged for the permission_prompt subtype only; idle_prompt / auth_success / elicitation* subtypes have no equivalent seam in a headless harness (cannot map).
- <a id="dev-hooks.post-tool-batch"></a>`hooks.post-tool-batch` — downgrade: Not bridged — the dsh tool pipeline has no per-batch emit point yet (hook-bridge follow-up).
- <a id="dev-hooks.pre-compact"></a>`hooks.pre-compact` — upstream-blocked (upstream_dependency: precompact-seam): Needs an upstream compaction-waterfall interception seam in dsh-compaction (planned).
- <a id="dev-hooks.pre-tool-use"></a>`hooks.pre-tool-use` — downgrade: Bridged with matcher support and the permissionDecision decision contract, but additionalContext is ignored, bounding hook-based pre-tool shaping.
- <a id="dev-hooks.setup"></a>`hooks.setup` — downgrade: Bridged as a first-run approximation, not the full upstream Setup contract.
- <a id="dev-hooks.user-prompt-expansion"></a>`hooks.user-prompt-expansion` — downgrade: Not bridged — no dsh emit point for prompt-template expansion.
- <a id="dev-commands.agents"></a>`commands.agents` — downgrade: Slice 0 MVP: thin snapshot (list/detail/stop) over listChildren + agents + resumePinStore; groups are residency-only (Working / Idle / Ready — no Blocked/Done); /agents attach is a reserved, unimplemented namespace. The TUI local-slash surface consumes the same ccAgents snapshot and ADDS fold-derived decorations (provider, prompt excerpt, last stopReason) to the detail view; the thin preset surface vs the decorated TUI surface is a deliberate divergence, never different ids or ordering.
- <a id="dev-commands.branch"></a>`commands.branch` — downgrade: Forks and reports the child id; switching to the child requires a restart.
- <a id="dev-commands.config"></a>`commands.config` — downgrade: Text-only render/patch with an allowlisted key set, not an interactive editor.
- <a id="dev-commands.exit"></a>`commands.exit` — non-goal: Host-owned by design; the dsh-native equivalents are the TUI /exit command (packages/ui/tui/src/slash.ts) and the idle double Ctrl+C gesture, so a preset-side port is out of parity scope.
- <a id="dev-commands.init"></a>`commands.init` — downgrade: Drives a follow-up turn that writes/refreshes CLAUDE.md rather than the upstream one-shot initializer flow.
- <a id="dev-commands.model"></a>`commands.model` — non-goal: Host-owned by design; the dsh-native equivalents are the TUI-local /model and /effort commands (packages/ui/tui/src/slash.ts, model-catalog) plus the ccModelRoutes alias service, so a preset-side port is out of parity scope.
- <a id="dev-commands.plugin"></a>`commands.plugin` — downgrade: No interactive menu UI (text output only); a static trust-warning line instead of interactive consent prompts; CC-only subcommands not implemented (details/eval/init/prune/tag/validate, --config, --sparse, managed scope).
- <a id="dev-commands.resume"></a>`commands.resume` — downgrade: Lists sessions; switching is host-owned (dsh --resume <id>).
- <a id="dev-commands.rewind"></a>`commands.rewind` — upstream-blocked (upstream_dependency: session-file-snapshot-seam): Needs the session file-snapshot seam; no checkpoint/rewind design exists yet.
- <a id="dev-commands.tasks"></a>`commands.tasks` — downgrade: Human-facing /tasks lists background jobs only; the todo-list seam is pending. The model-facing dsh-tool-todo and the TUI Ctrl+T todo panel cover the rest of the workflow. The footer cross-links to /agents (N background agents — /agents for details) when the ccAgents snapshot service resolves.
- <a id="dev-sessions.checkpointing"></a>`sessions.checkpointing` — upstream-blocked (upstream_dependency: session-file-snapshot-seam): Feature absent; requires a snapshot seam in the session layer.
- <a id="dev-memory.claude-md-imports"></a>`memory.claude-md-imports` — downgrade: The @path import machinery is absent — no parser or loader handles imports today.
- <a id="dev-memory.core"></a>`memory.core` — downgrade: Per-repo isolation (worktrees/subdirs share one store), shared global layer, memory_save as the save channel, recall reference-doc suppression, and opt-in team memory all work; CC's mtime-threaded recall and memoryAge aging are deferred until the harness FsInfo seam grows an mtime field.
- <a id="dev-skills.system"></a>`skills.system` — downgrade: Loader + base tool-skill, CC paths conditional activation, bundled subset (debug/simplify/batch), and TUI /name routing all work; CC's verify/stuck skills are not ported (ant-only; verify companion files absent).
- <a id="dev-subagents.task-tool"></a>`subagents.task-tool` — divergent: subagent_type dispatch over per-workspace .claude/agents (persona = definition systemPrompt, alias routing via ccModelRoutes, sanitized toolFilter, maxDepth 3, bundled explore/dsh-cc-guide agents, the bundled explore additionally carrying read-only serena symbol retrieval tools mcp__serena__find_symbol / find_referencing_symbols / get_symbols_overview) plus the continuable background loop (run_in_background, agentId-addressable send_message/interrupt/list). Deliberate deviations: fork + background is rejected naming upstream issue #2124 (fork stays foreground one-shot); no TaskOutput alias and no outputFile field; omitting run_in_background stays foreground unless the definition pins background: true, unlike Claude Code's interactive omit=background. Pinned defaults (repo-guarded): the repo agents deep-reasoner and fast-worker pin background: true, so omitting run_in_background on those Task calls launches them continuable in the background (the call resolves { status: 'async_launched' } immediately and the real result arrives later as a wake message — no inline result to compose on); run_in_background: false forces synchronous collection. Deliberate deviation: there is NO global omit=background default — the bundled explore and dsh-cc-guide agents stay unpinned and keep foreground first-epoch collect. Foreground collect refit: non-fork foreground calls (named agents and general-purpose) collect the child's first epoch INLINE as a continuable child — same pin preallocation, pre-start pin write, and tombstone-on-throw as the background path, so a foreground-launched child is pinnable/resumable exactly like a background one. The collector is a dsh-cc-INTERNAL parity instrument (bus watcher over subagent/start + subagent/end, one shared listener pair and watch map, matched by first-epoch runId; docs/plans/ 2026-09-10-epoch-collector-dsh-cc.md), NOT a Claude Code mechanism — declared deviations: (1) for inline-collected epochs the settlement account lives only in the tool result, not the parent session log (the duplicated subagent-settled notice is dropped by a pop-once pre-step filter; a promoted child is removed from the set and delivers normally); (2) on exec.signal abort the child is interrupted aborted exactly once via ctx.subagents.interrupt({kind:'ancestor'}) and the tool call resolves PROMPTLY with a synthetic stopReason "aborted" (never awaiting child quiescence; the real terminal arrives only as the suppressed notice); (3) a seam without interrupt degrades to a prompt resolve without child interrupt. Output schema gains optional backgroundedByUser: true (set by the Slice 3 promotion path, never by Slice 2 code paths). Ctrl+B promotion (TUI-only surface): while the dialog is busy AND the root-realm ccCollectorRegistry (published by the cc-subagent-task plugin, CcPlugins pattern) has ≥1 armed foreground collect for THIS session AND CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS is unset, Ctrl+B promotes EVERY armed collect of the session: the pending tool call resolves { status: 'async_launched', agentId, backgroundedByUser: true }, the watch is released (the runId-matched end later resolves nothing), the child is REMOVED from the suppression set so its settlement notice delivers exactly once normally, and the TUI echoes one status line. Pre-acceptance promotion (Ctrl+B fired while startContinuable is still in flight) resolves async_launched as soon as start resolves. Repeated presses are idempotent (a promoted collect unregisters itself; the second press is a consumed no-op). Declared deviations: promotion is a TUI-only surface — non-TUI clients have NO promotion path; busy Esc/Ctrl+C still interrupts (every registered collect of the session aborts exactly-once with a prompt synthetic aborted resolution); idle Ctrl+B is untouched (the editor's tui.editor.cursorLeft binding); under tmux, Ctrl+B is the default prefix — double-press passes a literal Ctrl+B through (send-prefix) and the Ctrl+X Ctrl+B chord is P1 (not implemented). Env kill switch CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS: a non-empty value other than case-insensitive 0/false disables the backgrounding-by-default pins (omissions collect in foreground) — explicit run_in_background true/false arguments remain honored both ways. Deliberate partial-parity deviation: upstream Claude Code's exact precedence for this env var is unverified, so the argument precedence is declared rather than asserted as parity. Capacity guard: the Task tool refuses a new continuable child (background OR foreground collect) when the parent already has 25 live children (listChildren entries with activity running) with the actionable error "parent has 25 live subagents; /agents stop <id> to release one, or let children settle" — a dsh-cc-side safety valve; Claude Code has no equivalent surfaced limit. Continuable cold resume: each background spawn captures a resume pin (resolveDetailed-selected alias plus maxTokens) into the resumePinStore service (preset row cc-resume-pins, isolated as resumePinStore in cc-services), and resume restores the pinned tuple INCLUDING explicit absence (a pin recording an unset reasoningEffort/maxTokens is honored as absent rather than re-resolved); a pinned model the parent can no longer resolve is gated by the subagents-resume settings namespace (subagents-resume.onUnavailableModel: block\|route-current, default block) with deny codes SUBAGENT_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE / WORKSPACE_CHANGED / DEFINITION_CHANGED / PINNED_TOOL_UNAVAILABLE / PIN_ORPHANED / PIN_UNREADABLE naming the policy knob — Claude Code has no equivalent mechanism. Spawn-time preload (dsh-cc-side, no Claude Code equivalent): an explicit `tools:` entry that is still a deferred MCP tool is activated through the duck-typed ctx.toolSearch seam at spawn, BEFORE the child starts, on BOTH dispatch paths — activation is process-global (every admitting agent's schema grows after the spawn); wildcard entries are restrict-only, deny/sanitize-excluded names are never activated, eager names are skipped, and outcomes surface in the Task result text (Preloaded deferred tools for child / Not preloaded: name (reason)).
- <a id="dev-mcp.config-discovery"></a>`mcp.config-discovery` — divergent: Deliberate dsh-first rule with no Claude Code analog: when a dsh-native config (the project .mcp.json or $DSH_HOME/.mcp.json) declares at least one server, Claude Code MCP config files are not loaded; skipped claude-only servers surface via a logger warn, a one-shot session-start TUI notice, and a self-clearing /mcp status line, and /mcp migrate imports them into $DSH_HOME/.mcp.json (raw entries verbatim, atomic write, .bak backup, existing names win). Escape hatch: mcpLoadClaudeFiles: true on cc-shell-glue restores the old all-merge behavior; an explicit mcpConfigFiles list bypasses gating entirely.
- <a id="dev-settings.migrations"></a>`settings.migrations` — downgrade: Mechanism only (version-gated runMigrations over an atomically-written settings.json, auto-run on mount) — no real migrations yet.
- <a id="dev-permissions.rules"></a>`permissions.rules` — downgrade: Rule engine + dangerous-command/path risk classifier, durable modes (default/acceptEdits/plan/auto/bypassPermissions via /permissions), plan deny with exit_plan_mode guidance, bypassPermissions pinning danger-full-access with resumeSandbox restore, and the always-allow derived-rule persistence all work. `auto` mode additionally gains an opt-in, escalate-only LLM risk-classifier stage: a one-shot auxiliary model verdict over tool name + rendered parameters (never tool results, input wrapped as an explicit DATA block the model is instructed never to repeat, quote, or follow), fail-to-ask on every classifier failure, `$defaults` soft-deny prose expansion, a verdict LRU cache, and durable `permission/classifier` session audit events (armed only when enabled, an llm service is mounted, and the alias route resolves). Read-only tool calls are exempt: they never invoke the classifier (the legacy auto path applies). Verdict parsing stays strict and fail-closed — a malformed output yields the constant reason "classifier output unparseable" (model output never reaches the modal; the audit record is digest-only). A per-route consecutive-failure circuit breaker (threshold 3, keyed provider/model) opens the stage for a failing lane: no further classifier calls on that route, one warn per process, one `breaker` audit event per session, reset by a settings change (rebuild). The breaker is restart-durable within a session: the first call of a session seeds the per-route streak from the durable log (attributed events only; a restored streak ≥ threshold opens at seed time). An open breaker surfaces one visible TUI fallback notice per session (live-appended `breaker` events only — never replayed logs), and caller-cancelled classifications are tagged `cancelled`, never breaker-counted. Raw model output is debuggable via the opt-in `DSH_PERMISSION_CLASSIFIER_DEBUG=1` process-log channel (`[dsh:classifier:raw]`, truncated to 2 KiB — never session events). Defaults: `timeoutMs` 8000, verdict budget 1024 tokens. The UI honors `permissions.defaultMode`: statusline, session switch, Shift+Tab cycle start, and the /permissions picker all fall back to the live merged settings default (fold precedence — a recorded session mode still wins), with the cycle clamped to its members. Settings-surface deviation: the auto-mode section is delivered as `permissions.autoMode` — an `autoMode` key inside the existing `permissions` namespace (camelCase key in a kebab namespace, like `defaultMode`), NOT Claude Code's root-level `autoMode` key, because top-level settings namespaces must be kebab-case upstream. Other documented CC auto-mode divergences (explicit ask rules still proxied to allow in auto; same-source allow-before-deny) remain recorded as unfixed follow-ups — they are not addressed or masked here. Remaining vs CC: managed/enterprise remote settings, UI mode cycle; the upstream permission/mode catalog pin is an upstream polish.
- <a id="dev-models.aliases"></a>`models.aliases` — downgrade: Frontmatter aliases (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable + dsh lanes + open set), settings model-aliases overlay with null-delete and builtin fallback, shared toAgentOptions per-field inheritance, and the ccModelRoutes service all work. Follow-ups: the /model command, ANTHROPIC_* env vars (no Anthropic semantics), and aliasing the main-session default model.
- <a id="dev-ux.statusline"></a>`ux.statusline` — downgrade: The command's stdout is rendered as multiple status-line rows capped at 3 (CC renders every row as its own status-line row); when the custom statusline is active, dsh-cc appends one client-drawn row below the command output carrying the permission mode + key hints (`<mode> · shift+tab · /quit`) — the stdin payload carries no permission-mode field (CC's doesn't either; CC renders that row as its own chrome). A 60 s hard run cap and a 64 KiB stdout cap are enforced (CC documents no timeout), and no debug-mode failure output is logged for the statusline command. The stdin payload omits fields with no truthful runtime source: version, output_style.name, worktree, workspace.git_worktree, workspace.repo, session_name, prompt_id, fast_mode, thinking, vim, agent, pr, cost.total_cost_usd / total_api_duration_ms / total_lines_* — context_window.current_usage IS emitted with CC field names (input_tokens / output_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens), truthfully sourced from the harness token usage projection's last-step buckets; steps cancelled or failed mid-flight may leave partial usage in that snapshot (documented staleness). used_percentage / remaining_percentage are derived from the currentUsage context length when present (fallback: the projected pressure sample; omitted when neither source exists). display_name duplicates model.id; exceeds_200k_tokens uses the currentUsage context length and is omitted when no occupancy source exists. transcript_path points at the dsh-cc-maintained CC-shape plaintext transcript mirror when it is ready (see ux.statusline-cc-transcript). hideVimModeIndicator is parsed but behaviorally inert (no vim mode yet); disableAllHooks / allowManagedHooksOnly gating keys are unimplemented. External settings.json edits apply at the next boot (no file watcher; in-process settings commits react immediately). refreshInterval is honored in seconds with a minimum clamp of 1.
- <a id="dev-ux.statusline-cc-transcript"></a>`ux.statusline-cc-transcript` — divergent: When the custom statusline is active, dsh-cc maintains a CC-shape plaintext transcript mirror at $DSH_HOME/tui/cc-transcripts/<sessionId>.jsonl (assistant usage lines + user anchor lines, atomic rebuild on bind/rebind, seq-watermarked appends) and the statusline payload's transcript_path advertises the mirror only once it is ready (>=1 usage line), instead of the dsh zstd-compressed private-format session artifact that CC-shape consumers cannot parse. The mirror is a filtered projection (usage + anchor lines only), not a full transcript. Hook payloads (packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/payloads.ts) still point transcript_path at the dsh session artifact.

## Upstream dependencies

### session-file-snapshot-seam — Session file-snapshot seam

**Problem:** dsh sessions persist a jsonl/sqlite projection; there is no per-prompt snapshot store of edited files to anchor a rewind against.

**Claude Code contract:** Every prompt checkpoints files about to be edited; /rewind (or Esc Esc) restores code, conversation, or both; checkpoints persist across resumed sessions and do not cover Bash-side changes.

**Refs:**
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing

### schedule-cron-selector — Cron-expression selector for dsh-schedule

**Problem:** dsh-schedule supports after_seconds / at / every_seconds (>=300s) but has no cron-expression selector, so ScheduleCronTool parity is unreachable.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code scheduled reminders accept cron expressions as selectors.

### webfetch-ssrf-allowlist — DNS-pin SSRF for web-fetch-http

**Problem:** The CLI now mounts @dsh-cc/web-fetch-http (literal hostname/IP gate). The remaining gap is DNS-pin / per-hop re-validation inside harness web-fetch-http.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code WebFetch enforces an SSRF allowlist before honoring fetches.

### precompact-seam — PreCompact interception seam in dsh-compaction

**Problem:** dsh-compaction has no interception point where a user-configured hook could run before compaction fires, so the PreCompact event cannot bridge.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code fires PreCompact hooks before automatic or manual compaction, letting hooks inject or transform context.

### tasks-todo-seam — Human-facing todo-list seam for /tasks

**Problem:** dsh-tool-todo is model-facing and the TUI renders the todo panel, but human-facing /tasks still lists background jobs only.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code's /tasks surfaces the session todo list to the human user.

### memory-fsinfo-mtime — Memory freshness — FsInfo mtime seam

**Problem:** CC threads mtimeMs through recall and ages memories (memoryAge); the current dsh-fs seam does not expose mtime, so both are deferred.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code memory recall orders by file mtime and exposes a memoryAge signal so stale memories age out of prominence.

### notification-seam — Notification seam in deepseek-harness

**Problem:** No notification seam exists in deepseek-harness (bell/OS/iterm); shipping notifications needs a new design.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code emits desktop/terminal notifications for attention-needed moments (bell, OS notification, iTerm2 escape sequences).

### permission-mode-catalog-pin — Upstream catalog pin of permission/mode session events

**Problem:** The plugin registers permission/mode into KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES via a runtime Set.add at load; bumping the harness's own compiled catalog is an upstream polish.

**Claude Code contract:** Permission-mode session state persists across process restarts, not just within the registering process.

### upstream-issue-2124 — Upstream harness issue

**Problem:** Fork children remain foreground one-shot until upstream harness issue #2124 resolves; fork + run_in_background is rejected with an error naming the issue.

**Claude Code contract:** Claude Code Task supports the fork provider in continuable background mode with the same agentId-addressable loop as spawn.

## Renamed capabilities

_None._
